reforms.description: The Energy Policy Act of August 2005 includes provisions to strengthen electric transmission system reliability through the establishment of an Electric Reliability Organisation to develop and enforce mandatory reliability standards. Additionally, the Administration's Climate Change Plan aims to cut the emissions intensity of output by 18% over ten years, promoting research into breakthrough technologies for GHG reduction.
reforms.package_name: Energy Policy and Climate Change Initiatives
reforms.component_name: Electric Reliability Organisation and GHG Reduction Research
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The reforms aim to enhance energy reliability and promote research into technologies that reduce greenhouse gas emissions, which can lead to increased innovation and productivity in the energy sector.
reforms.status_evidence: The Energy Policy Act and the Climate Change Plan have been enacted and are currently in force.
reforms.importance_rationale: The establishment of an Electric Reliability Organisation and the significant climate change initiatives represent major structural changes in energy policy.
reforms.source_quote: The Energy Policy Act of August 2005 includes provisions to strengthen electric transmission system reliability through the establishment of an Electric Reliability Organisation to develop and enforce mandatory reliability standards.

reforms.description: The National Energy Policy proposed expanding the use of nuclear power and funding research on cleaner burning coal technologies.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Funding research on cleaner technologies can lead to advancements in energy production and environmental sustainability, supporting economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The National Energy Policy has been enacted and is currently in force.
reforms.importance_rationale: While significant, the proposed reforms are not as transformative as the establishment of the Electric Reliability Organisation.
reforms.source_quote: The plan pledged to ease the regulatory climate facing energy producers, including environmental protection rules, and to provide tax credits and research support for a variety of energy-related projects.

reforms.description: The FY2006 budget proposal continues strong support for research and development in alternative energy sources and extends incentives for hybrid and fuel-cell vehicles.
reforms.package_name: FY2006 Budget Proposal for Energy R&D
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Continued support for R&D in alternative energy sources is expected to foster innovation and development in the energy sector, contributing to economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The budget proposal has been presented but not yet implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: While it supports important initiatives, the budget proposal is an extension of existing support rather than a major reform.
reforms.source_quote: The FY2006 budget proposal continues strong support for such research and development and extends incentives for the purchase of hybrid and fuel-cell vehicles.
